LESSON: ESTABLISHING AGRICULTURAL ENTERPRISE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: Agricultural Technologies and Entrepreneurship
Topic 3.3: Establishing Agricultural Enterprise
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 13

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Establishing Agricultural Enterprise, part of Agricultural Technologies and Entrepreneurship in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 AGRICULTURE.

Key inquiry question: How do we establish an agricultural enterprise?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Establishing Agricultural Enterprise together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
58

● Integrity: learner develops honesty when discussing legal or acceptable ways of mobilising capital to establish an

agricultural enterprise.

● Respect: learner understands and appreciates others when discussing and making presentations on factors of production in

an agricultural enterprise.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Financial literacy: learner develops investment skills when discussing with a resource person way of mobilizing capital for

establishing agricultural enterprise.

● Consumer education: learner develops consumer awareness when evaluating various ways of mobilising capital to

establish an agricultural enterprise, for example, importance of reading carefully terms and conditions of loan agreements

from financial institutions to understand their obligations.
